citeAs: Clark, P., Cowhey, I., Etzioni, O., Khot, T., Sabharwal, A., Schoenick, C., Tafjord, O. (2018). Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge. arXiv:1803.05457.
creator: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord (Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence)
description: The ARC dataset consists of 7,787 natural science questions (multiple choice, authored for standardized tests), partitioned into a Challenge Set (2,590 questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based and a word co-occurrence algorithm) and an Easy Set (5,197 questions). Questions span grade levels 3–9 and cover a wide variety of knowledge and reasoning types. The dataset is accompanied by the ARC Corpus, a 14M-sentence science text corpus.
name: ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge)
rai:dataBiases: The Challenge Set is defined operationally by questions that two specific baseline solvers (IR and PMI) fail to answer correctly, which only approximates the informal goal of "hard" questions. Research scores can be dominated by the performance of simple algorithms, biasing work towards incrementally improving those algorithms rather than exploring larger AI challenges.
rai:dataCollection: Questions were collected from a variety of standardized test sources (e.g., ACTAAP, AIMS, NY Regents, MCAS, TIMSS, and others) through several months of extensive search and investigation. Questions are non-diagram, multiple-choice natural science questions authored for grade-school standardized tests (grades 3–9).
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions sourced from standardized tests including ACTAAP, AIMS, Alaska Dept Ed, CA Standards Test, FCAT, MCAS, MEA, MEAP, Mercury (anonymous content partner), NAEP, NY Regents, TIMSS, and others. Also includes the publicly releasable subset (~60%) of the 2016 Allen AI Science Challenge (Kaggle) questions.
rai:dataLimitations: The Challenge Set definition is based on two specific baseline solvers, which only approximates the notion of "hard" questions. Questions are limited to non-diagram, multiple-choice science questions for grades 3–9.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were filtered into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set using two baseline solvers: an IR solver (using the Waterloo corpus) and a PMI solver. Questions answered incorrectly by both solvers were placed in the Challenge Set; the remainder formed the Easy Set. Only non-diagram, multiple-choice questions were retained.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to drive progress in AI research on advanced question answering and reasoning, moving beyond factoid retrieval tasks. It aims to encourage development of AI systems capable of deeper language understanding and reasoning, which has broad implications for AI progress.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking AI systems on advanced question answering requiring reasoning, commonsense knowledge, and deeper text comprehension beyond simple retrieval. Intended as a challenge to the research community to develop more powerful QA methods.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: IR solver using Elasticsearch (with the Waterloo corpus) and a PMI (Pointwise Mutual Information) solver were used to partition questions into Challenge and Easy sets.

evidence.rai:dataBiases: Operationally, we deﬁne a Challenge question as one that is answered incorrectly by both of two baseline solvers, described below. Although this only approximates the informal goal of it being a "hard" question, this deﬁnition nevertheless serves as a practical and useful ﬁlter, as reﬂected by the low scores of various baselines on the Challenge Set.
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: The ARC dataset consists of 7787 science questions, all non-diagram, multiple choice (typically 4-way multiple choice). They are drawn from a variety of sources, and sorted into a Challenge Set of 2590 "hard" questions (those that both a retrieval and a co-occurrence method fail to answer correctly) and an Easy Set of 5197 questions.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: Datasets are increasingly driving progress in AI, resulting in impressive solutions to several question-answering (QA) tasks... The challenge presented here, called ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge), aims to address this limitation by posing questions that are hard to answer with simple baselines.
